witnesses.title: Descending section with an implied edge selects the wrong elements
witnesses.counterexample: a = [1,2,4,8], n = 4: Fortran s1 = a(1) = 1.0, s2 = a(4) = 8.0, s3 = 0.0 (empty section); Python 15.0, 15.0, 15.0 (whole reversed array). Exact-model: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0046_refuted (Lean) exhibits `a(:1:-1)` on a 2-element array.

witnesses.title: FORALL is emitted as sequential nested loops (RHS of an element assignment reads the target)
FORALL scalar mask expression is dropped
ANINT is spelled np.round (round half to even, float result)
witnesses.counterexample: x = 2.5: Fortran 3.0, Python 2.0; x = -2.5: -3.0 vs -2.0. Lean: Recast.Exact.nintR_ne_roundHalfEven_example.

witnesses.title: INT(x, KIND=8) drops the kind: result saturates at the 32-bit limit
witnesses.counterexample: x = 3.0d10: Fortran 30000000000; Python -2147483648. The saturation is explicit code in `_f_int` (runtime.py:400-418), so it is part of the target's exact meaning, not a floating-point artifact.

witnesses.title: LBOUND is always 1 and UBOUND is the extent (non-unit declared lower bounds)
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran lo = 0, hi = 5; Python 1, 6.

witnesses.title: KIND(x) answers 8 for every real and 4 for every integer
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran 4; Python 8 (also for an `integer(8)` argument: Fortran 8, Python 4).

witnesses.title: HUGE/PRECISION/EPSILON/TINY answer for the default kinds only
Bit intrinsics are unbounded when the operand carries no NumPy dtype (literals, Python ints)
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran -2147483648; Python 2147483648 (also for a caller-supplied Python int `i`; with an np.int32 argument the runtime agrees). Lean: Recast.Exact.ishftK_example vs ishftUnbounded_example.

witnesses.title: INTEGER parameter of a companion module is typed 'not integer': `/` becomes real division
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran x = 1.0 (n/2 = 1); Python 1.5.

witnesses.title: Kind-suffixed single-precision literal hoisted as np.float64('text') (no single rounding); name collision across kinds
witnesses.counterexample: Concrete: 0.1 vs 0.10000000149011612. Exact model: both denote 1/10 (precision casts are identities), so the exact-arithmetic rule is sound; this is a concrete-execution discrepancy only.

witnesses.title: INTEGER ** negative exponent becomes a Python float
witnesses.counterexample: j = 2: Fortran k = m = 0; Python 0.5, 0.5. Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0020_refuted, FNP_R0024_refuted.

witnesses.title: Use-constants module spells integer quotients as Python `//` (floor) where Fortran truncates
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran -3; Python -4. Lean witness: Recast.Exact.tquot_ne_fquot_example.

witnesses.title: ASSOCIATE with a scalar selector: assignments through the alias do not reach the selector
witnesses.counterexample: x = 1: Fortran x = y = 2.0; Python x = y = 1.0.

witnesses.title: RESHAPE ignores ORDER= and PAD=
witnesses.counterexample: a = 1..6: Fortran b (column-major) = 1 4 2 5 3 6; Python 1 2 3 4 5 6. PAD: Fortran d = 1 2 3 4 0 0; Python raises ValueError (cannot reshape array of size 4 into shape (2,3)). Run: proofs/probes/reshape_order.

witnesses.title: PACK ignores VECTOR=
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran p = 1 3 30 40 50 60; Python raises `ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (2,) into shape (6,)` (loud); the value model has the target undefined where the source is defined.

witnesses.title: EOSHIFT ignores BOUNDARY=
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran e = 2 3 4 5 6 -1; Python 2 3 4 5 6 0 (confirmed by reading `_f_eoshift`; the concrete run aborts earlier at `pack`).

witnesses.title: MAXLOC/MINLOC ignore MASK=
witnesses.counterexample: a = 1..6, m = [T,F,T,F,F,F]: Fortran 3; Python 6.

witnesses.title: Character assignment does not pad/truncate to the declared length; LEN returns the Python length
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran n1 = 10, n2 = 3; Python 2, 6.

witnesses.title: Character literal with a doubled quote is emitted with the doubled quote (Python implicit concatenation)
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran value `it's` (4 chars); Python `it''s` (5 chars).

witnesses.title: Integer quotient nested inside a REAL constant expression is rendered as real division
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran 3.0 (7/2 = 3); Python 3.5.

witnesses.title: Constant expression with a negative integer exponent (constants module path)
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran 0; Python 0.5.

witnesses.title: NINT -> np.rint and MOD/MODULO -> np.mod in constant expressions
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran 3 and -1; Python 2.0 and 2.

witnesses.title: HUGE(<integer literal>) in a constant expression is spelled as the REAL inquiry
DIGITS(x) has no spelling and falls through to a subscript of an undefined name
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran: 53 for a REAL(8) x. Python: NameError at run time (the value model: target undefined where the source is defined). Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0089_refuted.

witnesses.title: Module-variable initializer `a/b` is rendered with true division
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran 0.0 (integer 1/3 = 0, then converted); Python 0.333...

witnesses.title: A scalar dummy assigned only under a condition is inferred INTENT(OUT): the caller's incoming value is replaced by the prologue zero
witnesses.counterexample: x >= 0 and ierr = 7 on entry: Fortran leaves ierr = 7; Python returns 0.

witnesses.title: _f_int_div uses a binary64 intermediate: int(a / b) is inexact beyond 2^53
witnesses.counterexample: _f_int_div(2**53 + 1, 1) == 2**53 in Python (helper executed in isolation); compiled Fortran int64 gives 2**53 + 1. Not a counterexample to the exact-arithmetic lemma (recorded per the handoff).

witnesses.title: Integer array division `_f_int_div(A, B)` and scalar-only intrinsic spellings raise on array arguments
witnesses.counterexample: Python: TypeError ('only length-1 arrays can be converted to Python scalars'); Fortran: elementwise truncating quotient. The target is undefined where the source is defined (loud, not a wrong value).

witnesses.title: Empty section with an edge below lb - 1 becomes a non-empty Python slice (negative-index wrap)
witnesses.counterexample: n = 3, a = [1,2,4]: Fortran 0.0; Python 3.0. Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0042_refuted (a 2-element array, source extent 0 vs target shape 1).

witnesses.title: WHERE evaluates the array RHS on every element before masking (exact-model definedness gap)
witnesses.counterexample: x = [0, 2]: Fortran y(2) = 0.5, y(1) unchanged; exact model: the target's `1.0 / x` is undefined at x(1) = 0, so the target is undefined where the source is defined. Concretely NumPy produces inf with a RuntimeWarning and masks it out: the observable values agree.

witnesses.title: HUGE(x) on a REAL variable that holds an integer-valued Python int answers the INTEGER huge
witnesses.counterexample: gfortran: 1.7976931348623157E+308; translation: 2147483647 (int). Lean: `FNP_R0087_refuted_realInt` (a REAL(8) variable related to the Python int 0).

witnesses.title: DOT_PRODUCT of INTEGER arrays is a Python float (accumulator seeded with 0.0)
witnesses.counterexample: gfortran: `idot 11 110.0`; translation: IndexError (`only integers ... are valid indices`), `_f_vdot(a, b) = np.float64(11.0)`.

witnesses.title: PACK of a rank ≥ 2 array returns the elements in row-major order
MAXLOC/MINLOC of a rank ≥ 2 array with ties picks the row-major first maximum
_f_seq_tail's rank-2 view drops the column remainder of a sequence-associated element actual
witnesses.counterexample: a = 1..6 column-major: Fortran a = 1 103 105 107 5 6 (a(1,2) = 4 + 103); Python: IndexError (index 2 is out of bounds for axis 0 with size 2). Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0057_refuted.

witnesses.title: A rank-2 dummy over a storage sequence not divisible by its leading extent raises in NumPy (partial trailing column dropped)
witnesses.counterexample: w = 1..5: Fortran x = w(5) = 5; Python: ValueError (cannot reshape array of size 5 into shape (2,newaxis)). Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0057_trunc_refuted, FNP_R0059_reshape_undefined.

witnesses.title: DIGITS of an integer literal in a constant expression answers the REAL value 53
witnesses.counterexample: Fortran 31; Python 53. Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0171_refuted_digits. Same classifier bug as FNP-D0026 (HUGE).

witnesses.title: A dummy whose intent is neither declared nor inferable is passed but never returned: the callee's write is lost
witnesses.counterexample: drive sets s = 'xxxxxxxx' then calls setname: gfortran gives s = 'hello   ', n = 42; the translation gives s = 'xxxxxxxx', n = 42. The INTEGER dummy `n` is inferred OUT and handled correctly; only the CHARACTER dummy is lost.

witnesses.title: RESHAPE with a source larger than the shape: Fortran truncates, np.reshape raises
witnesses.counterexample: a = [1,2,3,4]: gfortran gives b = 1 2; the translation raises ValueError (cannot reshape array of size 4 into shape (2,)). Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0102_refuted_shrink.

witnesses.title: Array bounds are re-rendered at every use: redefining a bound variable after ALLOCATE or entry shifts every subscript
witnesses.counterexample: n0 = 2 (`redef`): gfortran x = 0.0, lbound -2, ubound 2; translation x = 10.0 (`a[3]`, the element Fortran calls a(1)), lbound 1, ubound 5 (the inquiries are FNP-D0006). The same for a declared dummy `a(-n:n)` with `intent(inout) :: n` incremented in the body (`dummy`: 0.0 vs 10.0) and for an automatic local `w(-n:n)` (`autoloc`: 0.0 vs 10.0). Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0049_refuted (dims [(-2, 5)] allocated with n = 2, use state n = 3).

witnesses.title: ALLOCATE with the upper bound below the lower bound: Fortran allocates a zero-sized array, np.zeros raises
witnesses.counterexample: n0 = -1 (`basic`): gfortran size 0, lbound 1, ubound 0; translation raises ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed. Lean: Recast.Rules.FNP_R0160_refuted_empty (`F.execAllocate` clamps the extent to 0; the `np.zeros` model is undefined on the extent -1). The automatic local `real(8) :: w(-n:n)` called with n = -1 (`autoempty`): gfortran lbound 1, ubound 0, size 0; the prologue's `w = np.zeros(((n) - (- n) + 1,), dtype=np.float64)` raises the same ValueError.
